title: Relative quotient by a central subgroup of multiplicative type
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is an $S$-scheme with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams, as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. A reductive $S$-group is a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] group whose geometric fibres are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Unipotent means that in a faithful matrix representation every geometric point is a unipotent matrix. The centre $Z(G)$ is the subgroup functor of points commuting with all points after every algebra extension. A torus over $S$ is an $S$-group scheme which, locally for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of $S$, is isomorphic to a finite product of copies of $\mathbf G_{m}$. A maximal torus is a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] which is a torus over $S$ and which on every geometric fibre is maximal among subgroups isomorphic to a product of multiplicative groups; $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. Let $G$ be reductive and let $C\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed central subgroup scheme of multiplicative type: fppf-locally on $S$, $C$ is isomorphic to $D(N)=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_S[N]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $N$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Fppf coverings are faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. The fppf sheaf quotient $Q=G/C$, defined by sheafifying $U\mapsto G(U)/C(U)$, is represented by a reductive $S$-group. The quotient map $p:G\to Q$ has kernel $C$, is faithfully flat and finitely presented, and is a $C$-torsor: $(g,c)\mapsto(g,gc)$ is an isomorphism $G\times_S C\simeq G\times_QG$. The centre of $Q$ is the fppf quotient $Z(G)/C$. The map $T\mapsto T/C$ is a bijection from maximal tori of $G$ to maximal tori of $Q$, with inverse given by scheme-theoretic inverse image along $p$; every maximal torus of $G$ contains $C$. Quotient formation, the quotient map, this centre identification and the torus correspondence commute with arbitrary base change on $S$. No smoothness of $C$ and no restriction on residue characteristic are assumed.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2) and the quotient discussion in Lemma 3.3.2, printed pp.96--98; Corollary 3.3.5 and proof, printed pp.100--101; quotient interpreted as the represented fppf quotient, so its pullback remains that quotient and the quotient map is a torsor. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag supplies the reductive centre and maximal-torus assertions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-affine-multiplicative-quotient] to $(G,C)$: centrality implies normality. It gives the represented quotient $Q$, its smoothness, affineness, finite presentation, connected geometric fibres and the faithfully flat finitely presented map $p$ with kernel $C$. On each geometric fibre the same quotient theorem identifies $p_{\bar s}$ as a faithfully flat homomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-field-reductive-quotient] to it: $G_{\bar s}$ is reductive, hence so is $Q_{\bar s}$. Thus $Q$ is reductive.

The torsor isomorphism in [lem-sfb-relative-affine-multiplicative-quotient] has the asserted formula: if $p(g)=p(h)$ then $g^{-1}h$ lies in the scheme-theoretic kernel $C$, and $(g,h)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}h)$ is its inverse. These formulas are morphisms and inverse on all test schemes, not just on geometric points. The theorem also identifies every pullback $G_{S\prime}\to Q_{S\prime}$ as the represented fppf quotient by $C_{S\prime}$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.2; explicit kernel and torsor calculation.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel] applied to the reductive groups $G$ and $Q$ over the given Noetherian affine base, both centres are closed of multiplicative type and commute with arbitrary base change. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-preimage] to $p$ and $D=Z(Q)$: $E=p^{-1}Z(Q)$ is central in $G$, so $E\subseteq Z(G)$. Conversely, a section of $Z(G)$ maps into $Z(Q)$: after any further base change a point of $Q$ fppf-locally lifts to $G$, where the commutator is the identity. Thus $E=Z(G)$ as subgroup functors. Every section of $Z(Q)$ fppf-locally lifts to $E$, and two lifts differ by $C$. Therefore $Z(Q)=Z(G)/C$ as represented fppf sheaves.

We will use self-centralization also over the base: for a maximal torus $T$ of $G$, the inner $T$-action has fixed group $K=C_G(T)$, smooth affine of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-relative-torus-automorphism-fixed-group]. On each geometric fibre [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] says $K_{\bar s}=T_{\bar s}$. The torus $T$ is flat and of finite presentation over $S$, $K$ is of finite type over $S$, so $T\to K$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation]; as all its geometric fibres are isomorphisms, [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] makes $T\to K$ an isomorphism. Consequently $Z(G)\subseteq C_G(T)=T$, so $C\subseteq T$. The identical argument applies to every maximal torus of $Q$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.4, Lemma B.3.1 and self-centralization used before Corollary 3.3.5.

proof.text: For any torus $T\subseteq G$ containing $C$, fppf-locally write $T=D(M)$ with $M=\mathbf Z^r$ and also split $C$. The inclusion is, after further Zariski localization, dual to a surjection $M\twoheadrightarrow N$, by [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality]. Put $L=\ker(M\to N)$. The same node gives $T/C=D(L)$; [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] makes $L$ free of finite rank, so this quotient is a torus. Its map into $Q$ is monic: fppf-locally lift two sections to $T$, and equal images differ by $C$. It is a closed immersion by [lem-sfb-affine-multiplicative-type-monomorphism-closed]. Moreover $p^{-1}(T/C)=T$: lift a section of $T/C$ locally to $t\in T$; any other lift differs from $t$ by $C\subseteq T$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5 proof, pp.100--101; Appendix B character duality.

proof.text: Now let $T$ be maximal in $G$ and put $R=T/C$. Conjugation of $G$ factors through $Q$: a local lift of $q\in Q$ acts by conjugation, independently of the lift because $C$ is central, and these local morphisms glue uniquely. Restrict to the torus $R$. Its fixed subgroup in $G$ is $C_G(T)=T$ from step 4. On a geometric fibre, apply [lem-sfb-torus-equivariant-quotient-fixed-surjectivity] to the equivariant surjection $G_{\bar s}\to Q_{\bar s}$. Its fixed-group kernel is $C_{\bar s}$ because the action fixes $C$. Hence $C_{Q_{\bar s}}(R_{\bar s})=T_{\bar s}/C_{\bar s}=R_{\bar s}$ as fppf sheaves. Every larger torus centralizes $R_{\bar s}$ and is therefore contained in $R_{\bar s}$. This proves maximality of $T/C$ in $Q$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5, pp.100--101; using the fixed-group surjectivity explicitly instead of the phrase classical theory.

proof.text: Conversely let $U$ be a maximal torus of $Q$, and restrict the just constructed conjugation action of $Q$ on $G$ to $U$. Let $H=G^U$. By [lem-sfb-relative-torus-automorphism-fixed-group], $H$ is smooth affine of finite presentation with connected geometric fibres and is reductive. The action fixes $C$, so $C\subseteq H$ centrally. The restriction $p|_H$ has image in $C_Q(U)=U$ by step 4 for $Q$. Applying [lem-sfb-relative-affine-multiplicative-quotient] to $(H,C)$ gives a smooth affine quotient $H/C$ and a natural monomorphism $j:H/C\to U$: its kernel is trivial by the same local-lift calculation as in step 5.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5 proof, p.101: the fixed group and the map j.

proof.text: On every geometric fibre, [lem-sfb-torus-equivariant-quotient-fixed-surjectivity] gives the fppf quotient $G_{\bar s}^U/C_{\bar s}=Q_{\bar s}^U=U_{\bar s}$. The base-change assertions of [lem-sfb-relative-torus-automorphism-fixed-group] and [lem-sfb-relative-affine-multiplicative-quotient] identify this map with $j_{\bar s}$. The source $H/C$ is smooth and thus flat and of finite presentation over $S$, and $U$ is of finite type over $S$, so $j$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation]. Therefore [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] proves $j$ an isomorphism. Consequently $H=p^{-1}U$: if $p(g)\in U$, lift $p(g)$ fppf-locally to $h\in H$ using $H/C=U$; then $gh^{-1}\in C\subseteq H$. This is equality on all test schemes.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5 proof, p.101; Lemma B.3.1, p.288.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-central-multiplicative-preimage] to the faithfully flat map $H\to U$ with kernel $C$ and central multiplicative subgroup $D=U$ of $U$. Its preimage is all of $H$, so $H$ is of multiplicative type (and central in itself). It is smooth with connected geometric fibres by step 7. Hence [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-multiplicative-torus] makes $H$ a torus over $S$.

source.place: Lemma 3.3.1(2) and Corollary 3.3.5 proof, pp.96--101; Appendix B torus-recognition criterion.

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar s$, let a torus $V\subseteq G_{\bar s}$ contain $H_{\bar s}$. It contains $C_{\bar s}$, and the character calculation of step 5 makes $V/C_{\bar s}$ a torus subgroup of $Q_{\bar s}$ containing $U_{\bar s}$. By maximality of $U_{\bar s}$, it equals $U_{\bar s}$. The inverse-image calculation in step 5 then gives $V=p^{-1}U_{\bar s}=H_{\bar s}$. Thus $H$ is maximal in $G$. Steps 5 and 8 give both inverse identities $p^{-1}(T/C)=T$ and $(p^{-1}U)/C=U$, proving the stated bijection.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5 proof, p.101; direct use of the preceding steps.

proof.text: All constructions are canonical on test schemes. Quotient and torsor formation commute with arbitrary base change by [lem-sfb-relative-affine-multiplicative-quotient]; centres do so by [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel]. Therefore the equality $p^{-1}Z(Q)=Z(G)$ and its quotient identification pull back to the same equality and identification. The quotient $T/C$ also pulls back by [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality], as may be checked on its fppf splitting charts. Scheme-theoretic inverse image is a fibre product, hence pulls back to inverse image; fixed groups pull back by [lem-sfb-relative-torus-automorphism-fixed-group]. Finally geometric-fibre maximality is preserved by base change, by its geometric definition (or the self-centralizer test in step 6). Thus the two inverse maps on maximal tori are natural for every $S\prime\to S$, including non-Noetherian and nonreduced $S\prime$. No step required $C$ smooth.
